text:
lina: heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC cleanup the GH Actions SAST run flagged a bunch of duplicates and we also can’t find any KMS audit entries for the deployer SA. tagging @omar @raj for triage. repro/logs below, short thread please.

omar: seeing it now. SAST noise is mostly the same rule firing on vendored proto stubs and on generated clients — used to be suppressed by a scanner path allowlist that relied on the old service account ACL. after the RBAC change the runner cannot fetch the suppression list from the internal blobstore.

raj: can you paste the failing log lines?

omar: sure — from the GH runner logs:
```
2026-03-21T21:12:03Z scanner: failed to fetch suppression-list: access denied: Get https://internal-blobstore.company/scan-configs/suppress.json 403
2026-03-21T21:12:04Z scanner: artifact fetch failed: open /tmp/artifacts/xxxx: permission denied
```

omar: also checked KMS audit — looking for decrypt/encrypt calls by deployer SA around the deploy time (21:10 UTC) and nothing shows up in the key audit stream.

ab​by: fwiw, deployer SA was moved from project-scanner@ to infra-deployer@role earlier. That change removed a binding to the KMS key IAM. Might be the reason.

lina: suspected. raj — could the RBAC change have removed the KMS key binding or the keystore read permission? Which key should the deployer SA have? (we use GCP KMS for CI secrets)

raj: deployer needs cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key ring and also storage.objectViewer on the blobstore bucket. quick check commands:
- gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy --key=projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/ci-secrets
- gsutil iam get gs://internal-blobstore

omar: I can run those from my laptop if you want, but we probably should do it from the infra-admin account to avoid missing cross-project bindings.

dev-bot: ACTION: created temporary runbook ticket INFRA-1142 (ephemeral grant + re-run scans) — pinging infra-admins.

ab​by: mitigation plan: re-add the KMS binding for infra-deployer with a time-bound grant (1h) and re-run the GH action to let scanner fetch suppress.json, then re-evaluate SAST signal. If that clears it, we update the keystore policy with the correct SA principal.

omar: I can do the ephemeral grant now. Command (gcloud):
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/ci-secrets \
  --member=serviceAccount:infra-deployer@prj.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

raj: after that, confirm audit logs show a Decrypt entry from infra-deployer and that blobstore access is working. If audit entries still don't appear, verify audit sink config and that logs aren't being filtered by retention rule.

lina: note for postmortem: we should not tie the suppression-list fetch to a single SA binding. Maybe rotate to signed URLs or a repo-contained suppress file with limited read scope.

ab​by: agree. also suggest a pre-deploy check in the GH workflow that verifies key access and artifact fetch before running scanner step. tiny step to avoid noisy triage later.

omar: re-run results — with ephemeral grant the GH action completed and suppression list was fetched. SAST failures dropped from 48 -> 5 (real issues). KMS logs show decrypt by infra-deployer at 21:18:12 UTC.

raj: great. next steps: 1) patch keystore IAM to restore permanent binding for infra-deployer with least privilege and doc the intent. 2) add preflight check GH step. 3) open a small PR to add repo-level suppressions for generated code.

lina: agreed. assigning follow-ups:
- omar: INFRA-1142 runbook + quick patch (ephemeral grant now) — done
- raj: verify audit sink and add logging playbook (INFRA-1143)
- abby: GH workflow preflight PR and repo suppress file (SEC-2301)

ab​by: on it, will open PR and ping for review.

lina: thanks everyone :thumbsup: — closing thread once PRs are up; we'll include a short blameless note in the weekly security sync.
